system.name: ByteRobust
system.one_liner: A large-scale GPU infrastructure management system for robust, stable training of LLMs at ByteDance.

content.subject: how ByteRobust escalates a suspected failure from real-time checks through eviction, rollback, and replay to a diagnosis

elements.name: Real-time Checks
elements.role: continuous lightweight check that flags suspect machines, code errors, or no findings

elements.name: Infrastructure
elements.role: diagnosis result: the fault is traced to a hardware/infrastructure machine

elements.name: Evict Machine
elements.role: removes the suspect machine and reruns to confirm whether it caused the fault

elements.name: Stop-time Checks
elements.role: in-depth diagnostic check run when real-time checks found no suspect

elements.name: Reattempt
elements.role: policy action that reruns the job when stop-time checks find no suspect

elements.name: No Conclusion
elements.role: diagnosis result: reattempt succeeded without pinpointing a root cause

elements.name: User Code
elements.role: diagnosis result: the fault is traced to defective user code

elements.name: Rollback
elements.role: policy action that reverts the job to a previous code/checkpoint version

elements.name: Dual-Phase Replay
elements.role: policy action that replays execution in two phases to catch corner cases such as SDCs

elements.name: Human
elements.role: diagnosis result: the case is escalated to a human operator

steps.what: a suspect machine is found, triggering eviction
a code error is detected, sending the job straight to rollback
no suspect is found, escalating to stop-time diagnostics
in-depth analysis finds a suspect, triggering eviction
no suspect is found, triggering a reattempt of the job
the reattempt fails, falling back to rollback
the second eviction fails, falling back to rollback
rollback fails, escalating to dual-phase replay
replay finds a suspect, triggering one final eviction

content.key_idea: A single numbered pipeline escalates a training failure from cheap real-time checks through machine eviction, reattempt, rollback, and dual-phase replay, ending in a diagnosis or human escalation.
content.reading_order: Left to right along the nine numbered arrows, starting at Real-time Checks and following each guard label to the next stage.

palette.used_for: Entrypoint check nodes (Real-time Checks, Stop-time Checks)
Policy action nodes (Reattempt, Rollback, Dual-Phase Replay)
Diagnosis-result terminal nodes (Infrastructure, User Code, No Conclusion, Human)

style.arrows: solid black arrowheads, mostly straight lines with one curved connector

encoding.color_means: node category: pink/red = entrypoint check, blue = eviction action, green = policy action, yellow = diagnosis result
encoding.line_style_means: all edges are solid guarded transitions labelled with the condition (Have Suspects, No Suspects, Success, Fail, Have Code Errors)
encoding.state_means: shape plus colour: ellipses are check/result states, rounded rectangles are actions taken by the system
encoding.marker_means: circled numbers 1-9 give the escalation order of the decision path through the mechanism
encoding.emphasis: the escalating rightward chain (eviction to reattempt to rollback to replay) visually argues that ByteRobust exhausts cheap fixes before expensive ones
reusable_patterns: a repeated check-then-evict gate: an entrypoint ellipse feeding an eviction box that fans out to a result or the next gate
weaknesses: the same 'Evict Machine' and 'Infrastructure' labels are reused at three separate points, so the node name alone does not disambiguate which escalation stage is meant

evidence: The automated fault tolerance mechanism of ByteRobust.
combines real-time checks for immediate detection of common errors, stop-time diagnostics for in-depth analysis of complex failures
in-place reattempts to recover from transient faults, code rollbacks to revert from defective user codes

summary: This single wide flowchart depicts ByteRobust's automated fault-tolerance mechanism as one numbered escalation path. A pink Real-time Checks entrypoint either evicts a suspect machine (step 1), sends a job with code errors straight to Rollback (step 2), or escalates to Stop-time Checks when no suspect is found (step 3). Stop-time Checks likewise branches to eviction (step 4) or a Reattempt policy (step 5); failures there cascade through Rollback (steps 6-7) to Dual-Phase Replay (step 8), which either hands the case to a human or performs one last eviction (step 9). Every branch ends at a yellow diagnosis-result node (Infrastructure, User Code, No Conclusion, or Human), showing how the pipeline narrows a training failure's cause while minimizing human intervention and wasted GPU time.
summary_zh: 本图展示 ByteRobust 的自动容错机制：从实时检查出发，按编号依次判断是否驱逐可疑机器、直接回滚代码或重试任务，再升级到双阶段重放，最终将故障归因于基础设施、用户代码，或转交人工处理。
notes: Kept the prior 'walkthrough' grouping; the nine circled numbers plainly trace one ordered escalation path. 'Evict Machine' and 'Infrastructure' each label three distinct occurrences in the chain (after real-time checks, after stop-time checks, and after dual-phase replay); elements list each name once but relations/steps carry all occurrences.
